cards.verify: WVDOH design plans for the St. George bridge and approach overtopping elevation; Cheat River gauge rise rates, November 4, 1985.
cards.ask_next: At what stage does the St. George bridge approach overtop, and are responders told not to cross approaches once water is on them?

quotes.text: Well, the water just....a wave of water come and just washed us off the approach to the bridge.
quotes.speaker: Gary L. Lipscomb (Tucker County Sheriff)

quotes.text: They just finished that bridge this summer,
quotes.speaker: Keith W. Cordial (WV State Police trooper)

quotes.text: Yeah, it rained for maybe two to three days.
quotes.speaker: Gary L. Lipscomb (Tucker County Sheriff)

cards.title: Volunteer bass boat pulled residents from second-story windows at St. George
cards.place: House near the St. George bridge, Cheat River, St. George, WV
cards.note: A retiree used his own heavy fishing boat, pushed by waist-deep helpers over the bridge guardrail, to break into a second-story window and evacuate residents; his brother on the river had dismissed the threat earlier. (OCR-transcribed interview.)
cards.verify: Tucker County rescue logs and DNR/National Guard boat deployment records for November 4-5, 1985.
cards.ask_next: Which private boat owners did rescues that night, and is there now a roster or staging plan for them near St. George and Holly Meadows?

quotes.text: So we tied a rope to it and some of the fellows got in clear up to their waist and pushed the boat out, got it up to the guardrail where we didn't have to lift it too far.
quotes.speaker: Don Goss

quotes.text: And we broke out the storm window and tore the other window out.
quotes.speaker: Don Goss

quotes.text: "Auh, it never did get in up here," he said.
quotes.speaker: Don Goss (quoting his brother Leo)

cards.title: Riverbank trailer occupants waited; rescue truck drowned out
cards.place: Riverbank trailer below Seneca toward Petersburg, Pendleton County, WV
cards.note: Around noon, relatives in a riverbank trailer said they would wait. When they later asked for help, the rescuer's truck crossed water over its tires and then drowned out within 25 feet of the road.
cards.verify: USGS gauge records on the South Branch Potomac and North Fork in Pendleton County; county floodplain maps and trailer placement permits
cards.ask_next: Which manufactured homes sit in the riverbank floodway, and at what point should occupants be told the road out will close?

quotes.text: They said, no, they were going to wait a while because Aunt Pearl was catching water.
quotes.speaker: Roger Lee Morral, Sr.

quotes.text: When I went across, the water was clearly on top of my tires of the truck.
quotes.speaker: Roger Lee Morral, Sr.

quotes.text: So, I backed out and started out the driveway, and I got out within 25 feet of the road.
quotes.speaker: Roger Lee Morral, Sr.

cards.title: Debris blocked Hoot Owl Creek and Grundy bridges
cards.place: Hoot Owl Creek bridge and bridge behind Grundy, Buchanan County, VA
cards.note: Through the day, bridges at Hoot Owl Creek and in Grundy began to clog with debris, backing water up and over the decks. The narrator believes debris at Hoot Owl Creek was dynamited to keep water moving.
cards.verify: VDOT bridge inspection and damage records for April 1977; news reports on the Hoot Owl Creek debris removal
cards.ask_next: Who is authorized to clear debris jams at bridges during a flood, and what equipment and safety rules apply?

quotes.text: We were getting stories throughout the day that the bridges at Hoot Owl Creek and the bridge behind the Grundy were both beginning to block with debris in the channel.
quotes.speaker: Ronald Cole (radio station operations manager)

quotes.text: And the water was backing up, sloshing over the bridges, making them unsafe for traffic.
quotes.speaker: Ronald Cole (radio station operations manager)

cards.title: Night rescue: ropes could not reach, lights could not find survivor
cards.place: Holly Meadows, near Moss Bridge, Parsons, WV
cards.note: Fire crews could not get ropes to people on an overturned jeep; later, searchers' lights showed only tree outlines, and a motorboat crew made the pickup near dawn.
cards.verify: Parsons Fire Department and ambulance logs Nov 4-5, 1985; inventory of rescue boats and lighting available that night
cards.ask_next: What swiftwater gear, boats and lighting does the county now have staged on the Parsons side, and who can launch them at night?

quotes.text: When they came, they couldn't get any ropes to us.
quotes.speaker: Amy Renee Moore

quotes.text: They could see the outline of the trees and the outline of the trailer that was in the tree beside me, and that's all they could see.
quotes.speaker: Amy Renee Moore

quotes.text: They sent a man out in a motorboat to get me.
quotes.speaker: Amy Renee Moore

cards.title: Levisa Fork rises and falls within 48 hours, leaving no sandbag time
cards.place: Levisa Fork at Grundy, VA
cards.note: A lifelong resident contrasts the Levisa with slow Midwestern rivers; he says a strong storm upstream gives time only to move belongings and leave.
cards.verify: USGS Levisa Fork at Grundy hydrographs (time to peak and recession) for 1957, 1977 and 1984 events; NWS flash flood guidance
cards.ask_next: What rise rate or upstream rainfall amount should trigger merchants to close flood doors and leave?

quotes.text: But the Levisa, she’s altogether different. She’s–within forty-eight hours she can come and she can go.
quotes.speaker: Chuck Crabtree

quotes.text: If a storm front comes through and that front happens to decide to come north or south and it’s got a real punch to it, it can drop upstream maybe seven inches of rain.
quotes.speaker: Chuck Crabtree

quotes.text: When she starts rising and the water doesn’t stop coming down, you’d better shut your flood doors and pull out.
quotes.speaker: Chuck Crabtree

cards.title: Disaster assistance center lacked help for confused applicants; renters left out
cards.place: Disaster assistance center, Tucker County Courthouse, Parsons, WV
cards.note: A flood-recovery outreach worker says the assistance center opened two weeks after the flood with no one to help people who could not read or follow the system. Pre-disaster renters in FEMA trailers were told to find other housing, and a state housing program got few takers until a public meeting explained it.
cards.verify: FEMA DR-746 (WV) assistance center dates, temporary housing and crisis counseling program records; West Virginia Housing Development Fund flood program files.
cards.ask_next: Who will sit with applicants at your assistance center from day one, and how will you reach renters and people who can't read the forms?

quotes.text: But when they opened the disaster assistance center to courthouse two weeks later, people should have been there.
quotes.speaker: Ruth Ann Toth (flood recovery outreach worker)

quotes.text: They were pre-disaster renters. So, FEMA expects them to look for alternative housing.
quotes.speaker: Ruth Ann Toth (flood recovery outreach worker)

quotes.text: The opportunity was there, but no one really knew what it was about.
quotes.speaker: Ruth Ann Toth (flood recovery outreach worker)

cards.title: Firemen went door to door with four minutes to leave
cards.place: Kathleen Hall home, Parsons, WV
cards.note: A 73-year-old resident who had never left her home for a flood was evacuated by firemen who gave her four minutes and carried her down the stairs. Earlier she had seen the river rising and phoned a neighbor to move to higher ground.
cards.verify: Parsons Volunteer Fire Department evacuation records for Nov. 4, 1985.
cards.ask_next: Which streets did firemen reach door to door that night, which did they miss, and what did they tell people to take?

quotes.text: "Kathy, we'll just give you four minutes to get ready.
quotes.speaker: Kathleen Hall

quotes.text: They said, "You're leaving this time. You're not staying." I said, "I never have left my home."
quotes.speaker: Kathleen Hall

quotes.text: I said, "If I were you, I'd get my car and get up to your aunt's, in safer ground.
quotes.speaker: Kathleen Hall

cards.title: Dam buyout took small lots first; vacated homes were stripped
cards.place: Little Skin Creek, Stonewall Jackson Lake take area, Lewis County, WV
cards.note: A displaced owner says the Corps bought out house-and-lot owners first and larger farms last. As neighbors left, empty houses and barns were stripped overnight, and remaining residents guarded their property themselves.
cards.verify: Corps of Engineers (Pittsburgh District) Stonewall Jackson real estate acquisition records; Lewis County sheriff reports for the take area, 1979-1981.
cards.ask_next: In a buyout, how will you secure vacated properties and support the last residents left in a thinning neighborhood?

quotes.text: But they took the people that only had a house and a lot. They picked them off first.
quotes.speaker: Edith Bell Holden

quotes.text: Well, you'd go at night and come back the next morning and half the house would be gone.
quotes.speaker: Edith Bell Holden

quotes.text: I think it was up to each individual to protect himself.
quotes.speaker: Edith Bell Holden
